facts: OCX pins every dependency to an exact OCI digest, with no version ranges, no resolution algorithm and no auto-updates. [L8]
The dependency graph is a flat list of digests baked into each package's metadata. [L8]
A dependency digest must reference a platform manifest, never an OCI Image Index. [L12]
Pinning an index digest looks appealing because one identifier could then resolve to any host's platform. [L12]
Cascade publishing untags the previous index on every platform push, so an index-pinned dependency eventually 404s permanently. [L14]
Child platform manifests survive because every successor index still references them. [L14]
The project lock records per-platform leaf manifest digests, never index digests, for the same reason. [L16]
Publishers write dependencies tag-only, create resolves them into manifest pins, and push acts as a pure gate. [L22]
Push verifies that each pin already exists and resolves to a manifest, and makes no resolution decisions itself. [L24]
Enforcing the manifest-pin rule by hand does not scale, which is why the pipeline splits into create and push. [L26]
A package built with platform any can depend only on dependencies that also offer an any build. [L26]
A pin is a snapshot of the publisher's platform coverage taken when create ran, not a live query. [L28]
Pulling or installing a package fetches all dependencies transitively into the package store. [L32]

OCX sits closest to Nix in philosophy, with exact pins, no resolution, and a flat list of digests in JSON. [L44]
